If you notice that your functioning is getting worse, or that you’re getting more certain about unconfirmable memories, then reassess instead of pushing harder.

name: A-p131
text: If you want to deliberately do trauma-focused regression (going backwards in your memory or imagination to times when you were younger), or affect and somatic bridging (following associations from an emotional or somatic experience to find the origin of that experience, particularly if it was a traumatic experience you don’t know about), or if you find that you’re having substantial flashbacks or dissociative reactions, then you should do this with a trauma-informed clinician present. Make sure they’re trained in the specific method you want to do. Ask any potential person what they would do and how they deal with uncertainty and unexpected reactions. Note that even if you work with a person, hypnosis is not a way of knowing what did or did not happen to you.

name: A-p132
text: Note that having experienced trauma, crying, and even wanting to feel difficult feelings are not necessarily signs that you need more support than working on your own. You get to pick how wide or narrow a range you want to work in, but be aware that different people need different ranges. Pay attention to how you respond and what support you have. Feeling like you are handling it isn’t a substitute for having support.

text: Listen to your little one for as long as it takes until they’re comfortable enough to move closer to you. This is easiest to do if you’re making and keeping lots of small promises to your little one, so the various guards feel they can occasionally relax. Work on loving yourself in a way that your thinking doesn’t object to; work on thinking in a way that your love for yourself doesn’t become fantasy; work on doing this in the course of regular life so that your adult self can keep the promise.
